QUOTE: when `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` is not defined, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(foo)` expands to `private_foo`. When it is defined, it expands to `foo`. ... Anyone who defines the macro before including the headers gets the real names back.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that definers of the macro see plain names, while default consumers of the public headers see `private_`-prefixed names and get compile errors.
